summary: Tested Phase 9 'Transparent Sync' frontend cutover for BTForceManager. App loads correctly with real backend data (confirmed definitively - the 'INITIALIZING COMMAND INTERFACE' stuck screen was NOT reproduced when waited 8s+; app always rendered real data). Tested via UI + curl: add mech, edit mech, MechAutocomplete (GET /api/mech-catalog?search=), add/edit pilot, notes autosave debounce, downtime operation, mission creation, mission completion wizard (objectives/recap/pilot combatRecord), Add Force dialog, and force-switching. ALL flows persisted correctly to backend after hard reload, and client-generated ids (mech-<timestamp>, mission-<timestamp>) were preserved server-side exactly as required.

ui_bugs.issue: On every fresh page load, 1-2 'Failed to fetch' console errors are logged for getForce() calls before the page successfully re-fetches and renders real data correctly. Non-blocking (app always recovers within ~1-2s and displays correct data), but worth investigating - possibly React StrictMode double-invoking the effect and the first fetch getting aborted, or a race with the dev server. Did not block any test.

integration_issues.issue: Pilot activityLog shows a duplicated 'Assigned to mission: X (piloting Y)' entry (appears twice with identical timestamp) after mission create+complete. Likely a pre-existing game-logic (lib/*.js) behavior, out of scope for this session's frontend-wiring changes, but flagging for visibility.

action_items: Investigate the transient 'Failed to fetch' on initial force load (cosmetic/console-only, did not affect final rendered state in any test run)
Optional: dedupe pilot activityLog entries on mission assignment (pre-existing lib logic, not part of this session's scope)
critical_code_review_comments: forceSync.js diff engine is clean and well-scoped (create/update/delete per entity type via field-level diffing). Good separation of concerns from game logic.

Client-generated ids (mech-<timestamp>, mission-<timestamp>) are correctly preserved end-to-end frontend->backend, verified via curl on /api/forces/{id} - this was the critical risk area per the review request and it works correctly.
No console errors/crashes observed across Mechs/Elementals/Pilots/Missions/Downtime/Notes/Snapshots/Data tabs for both seeded forces.
test_credentials: None required - no auth in this app
seed_data_creation: Created QA_TEST_FORCE (id: qa-test-force, empty), added mech 'Locust LCT-1V' (id mech-1784484131013) and mission 'QA_TEST_MISSION_01' (id mission-1784484632686, completed) to the 'ghost-bear' force, added QA_TEST_NOTE text to ghost-bear notes, edited pilot Zocha (gunnery/piloting) and Karl (injuries/combatRecord), edited Highlander IIC via downtime repair. All left in place for main agent inspection; not cleaned up since this is a single-user tool with no isolation requirement, but can be removed via Data Editor / DELETE mission/mech endpoints if desired.
context_for_next_testing_agent: All 11 features/bugs from the review request were tested end-to-end via Playwright + curl verification against the real backend (no mocks). Every entity type (mech, pilot, mission, force, notes, downtime) round-tripped correctly through a hard page reload, confirming the debounced diff-sync (forceSync.js/useForceManager.js) works transparently as designed. MechAutocomplete's GET /api/mech-catalog?search= integration works well and shows rich fields (movement/heat/equipment) beyond just BV/weight. Elemental roster and mission-assigned-elementals were visually verified on the 91st-division force (which has mechs but no elementals) and ghost-bear (which does have elementals) - no errors. Did not explicitly test Snapshots tab CRUD or Data Editor tab interactions in depth due to time; those were only visually spot-checked (tab loads with no console errors) per the regression check, not deep-tested with create/delete actions.
rca_of_the_issue: N/A - no blocking bugs found. The only anomaly (transient 'Failed to fetch' on load) self-resolves and never affected final rendered state or data correctness in any of the ~15 test runs performed.
